Ugh and then there's the "concierge service" where they take all your deliveries and keep them for themselves. The Kathy that used to be there (I hope she isn't anymore-she obviously hated being there) called me names because I told her I need my package (that I'd had overnighted) that day, and she wouldn't stay past 5 to let me get it, wouldn't leave it at my door, and basically told me I was out of luck and they will never hold another package for me again, which was great, but then I guess when I had flowers delivered for me she changed her mind and decided to keep them for herself. But, the apartment was nice, and we had no issues with being charged for damages to the apartment like a lot of places will try to do even when you've done nothing beyond normal wear and tear. And the maintenance was ON TOP of any little issue I had, even when I needed help taking apart the drains because I lost a diamond down the pipes. Can't say the same for the contractors working on site, I got a couple flat tires from negligence leaving screws and nails in the road when a major construction project was happening. My fish tasted very fishy, as if it was on the edge if you know what I mean. I chalked it up to the large event and that they were just very busy. The third time was about a month ago my husband and I went there for lunch because I wanted to show him the motorcycle museum that is attached to the restaurant. The museum was fantastic, unfortunately it was the only thing that was. Though it was fairly slow our waiter kept disappearing for lengthy periods and returned smelling like an ashtray which was very unappatizing. I ordered the Katana Stir Fry which was pretty much deconstructed and not very tasty or appealing and I also ordered the soup trio which is their very best dish and it was delicious. Hubby ordered a burger and found it "average". Then there was this visit. My daughter and I were attending another event at the Chaivitz so I made reservations at Triumph (bc it is convenient to the chaivitz parking for women in uncomfortable shoes). We got right in to a table and that is where the fun started. Our server Ted was very good, I have NO complaints about him. But the food is another story. We ordered calamari and it was "ok" if a bit greasy and a small portion for the $9 price tag. I ordered the lunch thai salmon. For $15 I received a dry portion that could not have been even 3 oz. (it was smaller than a stack of square post it notes) it had no "thai" chili sauce, instead it had some green thick stuff on it that had no taste and was appetizing either. The cilantro rice looked like it had sat on my plate since lunch. The roasted veggies were ok, but how do you screw them up? The meal was not hot either. My daughter ordered the very overpriced special. $25 for blue crab cakes. The crab cakes were "very bready and less crabby" and didn't have a whole lot of flavor. They also were very dry. The pasta portion of her meal had less pasta and too much cut tomatoes and capers and the cream sauce had that coating on it as if it had been sitting there for awhile. I was disgusted. Almost $60 for a meal for two and it was pathetic. Eating out in St. Louis? By all means stop by their free museum here but skip the overpriced horrible food. Instead take the time to go to the Central West end or try one of the several better restaurants on Grand. I will never come here again and I do not recommend anyone else should either...I've given them more opportunities than I should have.

Well, we did....it was forgotten until we mentioned it and for the entire dinner time (and even when we left) we were offered the appetizer anyway or to get "to go" since it is "amazing"....we had ordered the "Homemade Perogies". In truth, the waitress was apologetic, so I won't be sarcastic anymore ;-] Instead, I'll tell you about my BEEF Stroganoff....I say it in this way because, unfortunately, I was SO looking forward to having it: Beef, mushrooms and homemade spaetzle...anyone who knows me knows I am putty in their hands with homemade noodles and saucy beef. Tonight was not the night for me....it was more Mushroom Stroganoff, which had a wonderful flavour and the spaetzle was really well made. The salad that came with the feature dinner was quite nice. My companion's trout on the other hand was very good and very well prepared....tasted like lake trout :-] and it was crisp on the outside and tender on the inside. Mine, on the other hand was quite good...the "Picrnik"...an apple spice cake which was moist and tasty (Not to be confused with the apple spice cake I had at the Wildflower Restaurant--hard as a rock). In all, we had a pleasant evening....however, if I return, I will order something else since having read some other reviews of CT, we should give it another shot...but for now, my opinion is what it is....okay in a serious pinch, but not on my top 5 list....

text: I was really looking forward to giving this restaurant a try. I have recently discovered Indian food, due to my wife being a much more adventurous eater who urged me to try it. I have also been re-kindling a lost romance with hot and spicy, and I figured that this would be the perfect place to test out my newly expanded palate. Before making the choice to spend our monthly night out at IndeBlue, I jumped online and read many reviews here and elsewhere that stated good, even huge portion sizes. There are reviews claiming spicy that's too hot to eat, and reviews that claim this is the best Indian food outside of India. Now, I'm a realist, but all of the positivity had me feeling hopeful. I was excited when we finally arrived at the restaurant. We arrived early on a Tuesday night and were the first customers. We were seated immediately and given water by the hostess. The floor and tables immediately surrounding ours were dirty with crumbs and dust. When the waiter appeared, he was very indifferent towards us. He brought our drinks and took our orders with no greeting or enthusiasm whatsoever. It was a quick, "What would you like to drink?" and later a curt, "Have you made a choice?" and that was that. He was definitely into the brevity thing. Now, I'm the quiet type, and I also understand that a person may just be having a not-so-great day, so I don't scrutinize or get offended. I just figured he was a little off his game and rolled with it. I'm also the last person to freak out over a few crumbs on a floor or table, but I found it odd considering they had only been open for about 15 minutes prior to our arrival. For our appetizer we decided to split the scallop special. This was simply labeled "Scallops" and described as Scallops and endive in an orange gastrique. For the entree course, I had the Chicken Tikka Masala (medium spice), my wife had the Chicken Korma (mild spice), and we ordered a side of plain Naan. Both entrees came with a side of Saffron Basmati Rice. The scallops and gastrique were excellently prepared. The scallops were moist and tasted fresh, the gastrique was very flavorful and provided a nice light tang to complement the richness of the scallops. I wished there was more, as the dish contained only three scallops. We wrote this off as being an expensive but tasty seafood appetizer and moved on. We were pleased that the food seemed to be so well prepared, and looked forward to our entrees. This is where it all goes downhill. The naan was $1.99. We got ONE 8" (-ish, I didn't pull out a tape measure) round of naan that had been sliced in half. It tasted excellent, but was severely lacking in its ability to appear as more than a singular, halved piece of flat-bread. Most restaurants, even the hoighty-toighty, jacket and tie, uber-fancy ones will give you bread with a meal; this one charges you for your bread and barely gives you enough to taste. This is especially painful with a meal that offers a great opportunity for the sopping of sauces that don't contain enough actual substance to fill a person. Each plate contained a bowl of 6 small chunks of beautifully cooked white meat chicken that had been drowned in its respective sauce and a little more than a handful of tasty rice artfully displayed on the plate next to the bowl. The chicken was bathed to the point of being invisible, and when consumed, left behind an almost full bowl of bland, un-soppable sauce. I could not discern any difference in the level of spice between the dishes. Both dishes lacked any heat whatsoever, and neither dish was seasoned very well. We found both to be very lacking in the spice department, which is the last thing that I expected in an Indian establishment. While searching for more chicken in my bowl, we were sprayed with a cleaning solution by the hostess who was wiping the table next to ours. My wife, who was wearing open shoes, was none too happy about this. We skipped desert, figuring it wouldn't be worth it. We left the restaurant hungry, unsatisfied and $55.00 poorer. To summarize, cost vs. quantity is a big issue. The poor service earns no points. Bland entrees didn't help matters much, nor did the hostess carelessly cleaning tables and spraying mystery solution at us while we were eating. On reflection, I have to wonder if the people that wrote those glorious reviews usually just snack all day and don't actually sit down to a full meal at any point. As for the comments about the level of heat, I decided that I had better stick to "medium" in order to avoid the inevitable sweating and possible embarrassing case of my tongue falling out or something equally as horrifying. I quickly realized that I should have risked it. The thought also crossed my mind that the restaurant owners may have read the reviews as well, and simply decided that they were giving away too much food and delicious spice for the horrible state of the economy. We will not be returning.

text: After all the great ratings on yelp from the other reviewers, we decided to try out Ekta (Fishtown). We're an Indian family, so while we may be pickier than some, most of the time yelp reviews have not steered us wrong. That is until we ate at Ekta. (For those of you that don't want to read the whole review, in short the service was poor and very slow, and the food was okay at best. I won't be going there again, and I would not recommend it). We came in for lunch (12pm) on a weekday, and the entire place was empty. Not a big deal since it is a weekday, so we decided to sit down anyway. The waiter brought the papad and chutneys to our table while we looked over the menu to order. The papad was good and crisp, and tasted fresh. The tamarind chutney was also very tasty (tart and not overly sweet), but the mint chutney, while it was spicy and not bad, had a sweet undertone that shouldn't ever be present when making mint chutney in the traditional way. Over all though, we were still enjoying our little snacks while we were figuring out what to order. We ordered the Samosa Chaat and Onion Bhaji as our appetizers. This is where our disappointing experience really began. We had asked for the chutneys and yogurt to be brought out on the side and not mixed in to the samosa chaat so that we could add those things in to our taste (a lot of restaurants make it too sweet for our taste, so it's just easier this way). Asking for all three of these things on the side was like a 3 minute conversation, so when they brought out the dish and it was soaking in chutneys but had the yogurt on the side, we were a little miffed, but understood that everyone can make mistakes and decided to try it and see how we liked it before we complained. That's when things just got worse. Samosas are supposed to be served hot... even when they are used in samosa chaat. The samosas in the samosa chaat we were served was cold... like straight out of the fridge cold. In addition, there was so much tamarind chutney in the dish that the samosa were basically swimming in it (not an exaggeration). So at this point we reminded the waiter nicely how we had originally ordered it, and since the samosa was cold if they could serve it to us hot instead. While the waiter admitted that most people serve the samosa hot and add all the cool/ cold ingredients on top, their restaurant did not and only served it cold. As a restaurant, if you have a microwave in the kitchen (which we know they did), why not just make a customer happy and heat up the samosa before serving it? I've never been to a restaurant that refused to accommodate the customer. In the end, they brought out another very cold samosa in the samosa chaat, and didn't bring out any chutneys to go with it at all, expecting us to eat it dry. On an upside, the onion bhaji was very good, but again they forgot to bring out the chutney accompaniment that goes with it, and we had to remind them to bring it for us. For lunch we had ordered the saag paneer and vegetables with unripe mango (can't remember the name, but it seemed really interesting) and two orders of garlic naan. After a while the waiter brought out the saag paneer and mango vegetables, but didn't clear our table first, so he had a lot of trouble placing things. When we stacked and collected our appetizer plates and dishes for him he took them away (another thing I don't usually have to do for a waiter to clear the table, which added to the poor service I mentioned in the first paragraph). We waited 15 minutes for our garlic naan to be served to us after he brought out our vegetables and it was only after one of us walked over to the door of kitchen/takeout area where the 2 workers where and asked about our naan since our vegetables were now getting cold. The response was "oh, do you only want 1 now?" Really?! 15 minutes is absurd when those items should have been brought out together since they are meant to be eaten together! Every other restaurant I have ever been to gives you all the portions of your entrée at the same time. Did I mention there was still no one else in the restaurant, so it's not like they were busy serving other guests. There also didn't seem to be many take out/delivery orders at the time since we were sitting close to the door and would have been able to see another customer or delivery person. The entrees we ordered were okay in taste and appropriately spicy for what we ordered. I would still prefer Tiffin, Karma, or Palace at the Ben to this place because their food and service are both good. If anyone was wondering, we were nice to the waitstaff despite the trouble and even told them our opinions as to how to improve service, but it didn't seem like they cared. All in all, I will not be going back and I won't recommend this place to anyone because of their poor/slow service and just okay food.

text: Let me preface this review by saying that I am a Vietnamese girl who grew up in Metro DC and so have higher standards than most for Vietnamese food. Okay, so hate is maybe a strong word, but I should have known I was being set up for disappointment because although this restaurant was packed during dinner time, I was the ONLY Asian person there who wasn't an employee. This is another one of those Vietnamese places that caters to a (white) American customer base. The waitress seemed friendly but very rushed and impatient at my group (boyfriend's family + me), who had brought me here so that I could make recommendations about what Vietnamese foods to try because they have little experience with the cuisine. The gist of my review is that the food did not taste right, and the service was okay (attentive but a bit rushed). You can stop reading here, but for details about the specific foods I tried, keep reading. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- We ordered the goi cuon as an appetizer, and I was a bit confused that it was served with nuoc cham (nuoc mam/fish sauce mixed with lime juice, sugar, and water). I'm used to having it with peanut sauce, but sure, whatever. We also got the spiced tofu (which the waitress recommended because she thought the dau hu chien don was "flavorless" -- her words, not mine), but I thought the tofu was flavorless regardless and the sauteed vegetables it came with were too oily and salty. Again, sure, whatever. The rest of my group ordered pho, and I tasted the broth--it was good but the flavor was a bit watered down. If there were ever a chance that I'd ever come back here, I would stick to the pho (having broken my cardinal rule of only ordering pho at a pho restaurant). But I ordered the bun thit nuong cha gio, and I could go on about all the things about it that irked me. It contained less vermicelli noodles than I am accustomed to (not a big deal since I wasn't all that hungry), and the nuoc cham had already been dumped in it for me. Every other Vietnamese restaurant I've been to brings the sauce out on the side so that you can put in the amount you like. I personally don't like my noodles to be totally drenched in it and soggy by the time it is in front of me. The pork was this artificial red color (I've seen this before, whatever) and seemed a bit undercooked. Parts were too chewy, too soft, too salty, too sweet... I just couldn't decide what was off about the pork, so I moved it aside and just didn't eat it. By the time I was almost done with the food, I felt a tiny bit nauseous from the soggy noodles and the flavors being a little off. So... I am not a picky eater and even if I don't think a Viet dish tastes "authentic" (hate that word), I can still enjoy it and think that it at least tasted good. But this is the first time I can honestly say that I really didn't enjoy something I was served at a Viet restaurant. While I'm sure there are other items on the menu I probably would think taste good, even if they didn't taste "right," the experience left me thinking, "Wow, I have definitely experienced way better." But I can't bring myself to leave one star because I love to see the Vietnamese community thriving, and the walls of the restaurant are pretty cool. So... two stars.

text: I am a Besh FANATIC. Or misses. In this case, misses by a long shot. We - my food-adventerous fiance, my meat-and-potatoes and visiting-from-NC-dad, and I (who will eat anything not nailed down) - arrive around 7:45 to a mostly empty albeit winsome and modernly-decorated dining room. Not necessarily the most encouraging scene, but it's Monday during tourism down-time. We're promptly seated, greeted by our very pleasant server, Carrie, and proceed to examine the retro-styled menu. Fiance orders a beer, the P-51. Out of stock - strike one. Tries again with the ever-classy champagne of beers, High Life. Out of stock - strike two. Orders a third beer, the Blonde Bombshell. Fortunately, this one was available, though not at first glance - it was hiding in the cooler, and was pretty delicious... not High Life delicious, but still pretty good. After drinks get settled, we begin a proper perusal of the menu - you know, the foreplay part of the meal that sets the pace for the entire dining experience. Even though I'd all but memorized the menu from the website, it seemed there were fewer options that I anticipated, and the stuff that was there seemed almost... gimmicky? Not bad, just not exciting. I love rabbit, and I love pate, so naturally the rabbit pate was my app pick. We also got the crab pies and, to my surprise, my dad opted for the gizzards. Technically, gizzards are meat, and my dad's a southern guy, so it made sense; whatevs. The pate arrived in a rations-style tin with an American Sector paper-wrapped sleeve of saltines. Clever, I guess, but not visually appealing: even though the texture is similar, I don't want to be served anything that even vaguely resembles cat food. And saltines? Really? I know it's not August, but still! Brioche! Wheat crackers! Crostini! A damn piece of tree bark! Not saltines! What can I say, it made me sad... and not just the presentation, but the flavor! It tasted, to me, like American cheese: very salty, very processed, and not at all savory as I was hoping. The fiance liked it, but he also likes plain slices of American cheese. The gizzards and crab pies were nothing special - not bad, not delicious, just so-so. We also ordered a bowl of gumbo to share which, as a soup, was pretty good, but as a gumbo in a city rife with amazing cajun and creole options, it was very ho-hum. Now for entrees! I realise that I've written an essay at this point, so I'll attempt (and probably fail) to keep it brief: Fiance - Beef short ribs. Good flavor, horrible execution. There was some sort of chipotle/arbol seasoning in the mac and cheese that went well with the beef, but unfortunately the macaroni noodles weren't completely cooked so it fell flat. Greens and additional jalepeno grits were tasty, but not enough to make it worhwhile. 5.5 out of 10 stars. Dad - Chicken-fried steak. A verrrry picky eater born in Mississippi, my dad is a chicken friend steak purist. Mushrooms in the gravy didn't make him happy, but he's afraid of vegetables and fungi, so keep that in mind. French fries were, in my opinion, delicious - pommes frites in need of a good garlic aioli instead of ketchup - but as far as he was concerned, the dish was lackluster. 4 out of 10 stars. Yours truly - Chicken and dumplings. My dad almost ordered this but then called an audible when he was informed that, rather than have the traditional biscuit doughy blobs of dumplings (gag) so loved by good ol' boys and girls, this dish had ricotta dumplings that were similar to gnocchi. Oh, and vegetables. He doesn't do squash, carrots, or green beans, baby or otherwise, so no thanks. I, however, am a huge fan of all of the aforementioned, so I went with it. It was okay... the presentation was fine and the dumplings soft and pillowy, but the chicken wasn't well-trimmed, so I kept having to remove knobs of fat and cartilage from my mouth. The veggies were perfectly cooked and al dente, but the overall dish seemed very thick and short on flavor. 4 out of 10 stars. By this point, I was very full, but the boys felt it necessary to power through dessert. A hazelnut-caramel banana split and vanilla/candied bacon cupcake made its way to our table. The split? Awesome. Bruleed sugar on a banana? Yes! The cupcake? Bacon for dessert? YES! Unless it tastes like a maple-sweetened Beggin Strip. Sad face... Maybe it's better and busier at lunch, but I'm not dying to return.

text: If you are donating, I suggest other places. I was instructed to pop in HOPE Thursday afternoon to assess a dog-friendly kitty . A shelter person who directed me to HOPE informed me to come after 12:00 noon . Since I had my well mannered (cat-safe) dog with me in the first shelter , I brought her along to help out with a quick and general temperament test at HOPE. . I discovered this is a building without a sign, or rules, or directions so when I opened the door, I hadn't any idea there wasn't a reception desk nearby. Instead we quickly passed the dog kennels. There were cats on the floor and there was no double safety cage or double protective door at the main entrance. My dog went into a corner in the back and was in a down position. I noticed a wonderful kitty nudging my dog with affection. My dog did not " mingle"with other cats and was later separated outside. Later, I took my dog home , grabbed my husband from work and came back for my husband's opinion at 4:00 pm . The volunteer stated the place had just closed exactly at four and she did not give us five minutes. Later, I received an e-mail after attempting to make an appropriate appointment with the manager. This is what HOPE's manager wrote: " I was very upset to hear that you brought your dog to the shelter and let him mingle with the cats. You should understand that this is not something that we ever allow. Also, we do have specific hours and are not open during the week. I do not believe in clicker training or agility training for cats so I don't feel we would be the right place for you to adopt from. " Too bad the rules were not on the door. Too bad the place is closed from Monday through Friday. Too bad the main door was unlocked without a doorbell. For those new to cat behavior, "clicker training" for cats is for enrichment purposes only. Clicker trainers use positive reinforcement ( treats!) to teach cats fun games to encourage intelligence , create trust, promote exercise ( hopping over hurdles!), maintain a healthy weight, prevent behavioral problems, and to promote closer relationships . That's about it. Nevertheless, it's no big deal if the cat would rather hang out or do something else. Too bad Susan mentioned she does not believe in this kind of enrichment. Too bad the manager was quick to form negative impressions of humans who actually have a great home environment and want to help.

text: Will preface with stating, maybe I am too picky, maybe I taste sweet more potently than most. Also as I try other items on menu, will update review as I realize my spouse and I can only eat so much each time and it won't be such a thorough review. However, I doubt we'd return to Fork. We had been wanting to try this place just for the convenient location and interesting online menu, but foodie friends had given lackluster reviews. Today was just so nice and sunny, yet windy enough to keep us cool that we decided to try the outside seating. Indeed, the weather was perfect for outside, given the lack of shade, except that the Hole is finally being worked on. Due to poor tarping, tiny styrofoam bits were blowing in, through, and upon the patio. yum. Once it gets hotter and less windy, look out! They will need some shade or trees and misting fans, because that is going to be stinking hot. Server very nice, timeliness of order taking, delivering, checking on all fine. Easy to be seated. Decided on the fried asparagus for starters, came with a very nice buttermilk ranch dipping sauce. I would say their frying oil temp is set too low, as the breading was greasy and not very crisp. Flavors good, asparagus was perfectly cooked. Despite that, so much grease = meh. Drinks: it is brunch, so ok for a few cocktails. Spouse got the bourbon-based 'old fashioned city bank.' This was a good combination, multiple ingredients but the bourbon still had good flavor. Too bad I'm not a bourbon fan, as my cocktail was too damn sweet and had hardly any alcohol. Mine was the 'Z's bucket,' a gin/berries/basil/lemon. Actually felt the flavor more like a pink lemonade with barely a shot of gin, in at least an 8oz glass. Disappointing and boring. In fact, ALL the cocktails on the list that didn't have bourbon (ok, leaving the mojito and the bloody mary off the list because I don't order those) came across as girlie drinks, and seemed likely to be super sweet. No adult drinks featuring liquor other than bourbon. Not adequate for me! Go to redfeather, get lamplighter. Husb had a burger with the rosemary/parm fries. The fries were good, he liked the burger, though the patty too small for the oversized bun. Since I am sooo picky..do go try this place if you at all want to, but below is the bulk of my negativity! I had the chicken corn chowder. For some reason I assumed the soup, listed as containing chicken, would not have bacon. I hate bacon/pancetta, I avoid pork and ham, but will eat if the flavor isn't overwhelming. Therefore if something lists bacon, I won't order. So I ordered the chowder, which doesn't list pork product on the menu. Oh look, has bacon. I didn't send back because...oh look, almost no bacon flavor. People! If it has bacon, you need to list it on the menu. DUH. And if you are going to use bacon, it needs to be enough to come across when the dish is eaten, otherwise it's a wasted ingredient, and there's the odd kosher person who will be pissed! Beyond the random flavor attempt, it came out not very hot. What was good was the large chicken chunks, the nice potatoes, and the corn flavor. I think it had some added thickener though, a little weird on the texture. I also ordered the cheese plank. The menu states: "*Northwest Cheese Plank 10.75 ~ assortment of local hand-crafted cheeses, local stone fruits, City Peanut Shop's spiced pecans & Ahaus Beehaus honey" Now you see where I'm a giant snob. This just looked sad. It wound up being about 1/2 oz manchego, a ~#50 scoop of chevre-type goat cheese, 1 oz hard goat, and 1 oz MILD white cheddar with some sort of truffle flavor. A few very thin slices of some local pear (this was so thin it rolled around the chevre fairly well, just not enough of it), probably 3 sliced up dried apricots, 3 small torched slices of bread (these crumbled to touch, wrong variety used), one very sad strawberry (but flavor good, especially for March). For the price, NOT WORTH IT. Go to Co-op, get better cheese, spend $3. Or even Freddy's, they have a surprising cheese selection. Oh, the spiced pecans were fine. Not super, sweet and spicy is about it. Maybe 2 tablespoons there. I was reluctant to order the cheese plate due to the bit about the truffle flavor, as I dislike truffle oil, but it actually didn't come through at all. This one was boring. I like a stronger, drier, more English cheddar, and this was moist and mild. The honey is one I've had several times, you can even just buy it if you can find it, and it's great honey. But why put it over the manchego? What? That needed to be on the side. The manchego itself was fine, just oddly sweet for some reason, and really a very parsimonious portion. The hard goat was ok, probably the most interesting sample, but not that interesting in terms of...cheese. Chevre fine. Would come back for a pretty good burger if wanted cocktails (don't suppose a plain martini can be too sweet?), otherwise just go to 5 guys for a burger.

It was taking so long that I began to worry about how painful the order process was going to be. I was surprised when it was very quick. The burgers. They weren't bad, but they weren't good either. Both were ordered medium yet were two completely different shades of pink in the middle. It was more like one medium-rare, and one medium-well rather than two medium burgers. The bun of my "Philadelphia Burger" turned to a soggy goop almost by the time it arrived, and the goat cheese on my wife's "Napa Valley Burger" wasn't even spread around and instead was just a clump on it. The seating. It's all bolted to the ground, and while that does't seem like a huge problem it becomes one when you have a toddler in tow. There's not many good spots where you can put a high chair and be in the reach of both parents. Not the worst of worst, but annoying. The bad: The fries. The fries were a mixture of over-done, and soggy. There were a few in there that were the "golden-brown crispy on the outside soft-on-the-inside" nirvana, but they were few and far between. This, to me, was the unforgivable part. Bobby Flay spends much of time talking about how to make the perfect fry, how much care he puts into his fries, and so on. I expected better. I expected a lot better. The noise. This place is loud. Not mildly loud, but loud loud. Between the open kitchen and strangely-loud radio it just isn't a place to have a quiet meal. Overall, there are a lot better burger joints out there and for a lot better price. It's not my dislike of Bobby Flay that makes me dislike this place, it's my dislike for over-priced inferior food.

text: I had the honor of seeing this place untouched the morning it opened. No one was there--it was a ghost town for the most part. This was great because I got to talk with the shop keepers and owners. Oxford Exchange is a great concept, done for the most part extremely well. It's almost perfect. I love how they've partnered with Teabella and Buddy Brew Coffee. Two of my favorite places now within a mile of my place. The bookstore is great, with many awesome editions of novels and classic literature in interesting covers you don't see everywhere. You can tell someone put their time and effort into almost every book there. A walk down a long hallway opens to a central seating area with tables, couches, chairs and more. On either side of the building sits Buddy Brew and Teabella, each serving their locally famous concoctions. I love the Cold Brewed Frothy top at Buddy Brew and iced Silver Needle (or hot depending on the weather--we're in Florida for crying out loud). One problem here--Oxford exchange has this idea that by not offering free Wi Fi to "standard guests" they will somehow create a more conversational environment. Haven't they heard of 4g? This is a dumb move in my opinion that will only hurt Buddy Brew and Teabella. No reason not to offer Free Wifi. I'd love to stop in during the morning and get some work done and enjoy some tea or coffee, but in order to have access to WiFi, you need to be part of the "club". I think this is a bad move. The wonderful shop towards the front of the building is so cool. It's a more serious version of Anthropologie, with interesting insect specimens, petrified wood, clothes, decorations, body care and more. Really great store with a great view of UT. The restaurant in OE is okay. The servers sometimes seem to not know what's going on, but that may just be attributed to it being so new. Not to bring up the WiFi thing again, but it's funny they want to ban people from wifi while they've got their servers nose deep in an iPad while taking your order. Very impersonal, or maybe our guy was just slow. The food was okay. I got a Club salad that was missing the Turkey. Fiance got the grilled cheese--she loved it. It really was a solid Grilled Cheese. Overall, It's worth eating at. I would have to try some other dishes, but nothing really made my mouth water. Before the place started really picking up, I took my fiance and her parents there for High Tea. I found it to be very well priced. The tea was excellent, brewed just right C/O Teabella. We got the Silver Needle and I believe a Earl Grey. Scones, clotted cream, tea cakes, and fresh jam made for a nice afternoon in the Conservatory, a giant glass terrarium with a humidifying ancient stone fountain at it's center. Great environment for the moss, orchids and other humidity loving plants they keep in there. Very nice. In all, I think OE is a great concept that I'm proud to say is housed in Tampa. I think the restaurant needs to get to the caliber of the high end coffee and tea distributors that it's supposed to support. Definitely a place to go to often. I love it.

text: I used to eat Papa Johns all the time. It was one of the darkest periods of my life. I don't want to get into it here. Sometimes I still get a hankering for some shitty fast food pizza. I call Pizza Hut, Papa Johns or wherever, get whatever they've got on sale, and suddenly I'm reminded of why I don't #fuxwit shitty fast food pizza on a regular basis. Pizza Hut is probably the best of them, for what it's worth. Dominos is obviously the worst. Papa Johns falls somewhere in between. If the pizza at Papa Johns tasted like anything at all, it would be dangerous. Alas, the pizza at Papa Johns doesn't taste like anything at all. It's weird, because pizza isn't made of anything other than ingredients that you'd almost expect to be overwhelming: tomato sauce, various kinds of cheese, spicy meats like sausage and pepperoni, onions, black olives, so on and so forth. There's no way you should be able to put together any combination of those ingredients and not have it at least be offensive in nature. If the pizza doesn't taste like shit, at least my breath should stink. Is that not where the term pizza breath comes from? A pizza from Papa Johns tastes like a good pizza that's been put through a dishwasher. If you concentrate hard enough, you can detect a slight hint of what a good pizza is supposed to taste like. But mostly it's just kinda bland. It's not offensively bad in the way that Dominos is, and it's very consistent, and I suspect that this is why it's become so popular. If the tomatoes tasted like actual tomatoes, they wouldn't appeal as much to people who are really into ketchup. I got a flyer from Papa Johns a few weeks ago, towards the beginning of football season. I noticed they had some good deals going on during the beginning of the week, and I figured I should take advantage of them, because it's not like I've got shit else going on at the beginning of the week. You can get any pizza from Papa Johns, including specialty pizzas, for $11 all week long, but on Mondays it's only $9. They'll still try to stick you for $11. You have to mention that you have a coupon. Don't let Papa Johns rip you off. Don't worry, if you don't have the actual coupon. They don't ask for it when you go to pick it up. If they do, tell them to go fuck themselves and go to Pizza Hut. The pizza's better there anyway. Of course I had to go with one of the specialty pizzas, which would cost like $90 if it wasn't on sale. But here's something else to watch out for: I think Papa Johns is introducing a lot of so-called specialty pizzas that don't cost as much to make. These pizzas shouldn't cost that much anyway, because they don't have a lot of meat on them. Case in point, the new Classic Sausage and Peppers pizza, which I tried. It's just a sausage pizza with onions and peppers. It should be a proverbial party in my mouth (no Sandusky), because sausage, onions and peppers is a match made in fat man heaven, but it doesn't taste like much, because I think the sausage and peppers would taste better if they were more caramelized. But I'm actually more concerned with whether or not this pizza is worth as much as it would cost if it weren't on sale. For that price, you could get a pizza from a place that's a bit more "authentic."

text: To each his own--while I'm curious how anyone who isn't a vegetarian can give Central Grocery less than 5 stars, I won't dwell on it. Instead, my motivation for the five star rating: The muffaletta is a great sandwich and Central Grocery renders it perfectly. The bread is perfect. Their olive salad is perfect. The quantity of meat and cheese are perfect--it's like a blueprinted 440 six pack, only on modern Michelin's. This isn't a NY sandwich, where the goal is to see how much meat you can fit into the sandwich--it's about balance. It's a salty, cold (yes, muffalettas should be cold), wonder and it gives me chills to think that I can simply walk over there, any day (except Monday--today) and purchase one for fast food prices. Olive oil on my lips, the tang of salt in my mouth, and I have to resist running back to the place, jumping over the counter, and hugging the owners. They wouldn't understand. They're busy--trying to feed others. That would be wrong. I hug myself and the moment passes. I'm not exaggerating. It's that good. And it's consistently good. OK, I lied. I am dwelling. Some rebuttals are in order: Yes, the lines are long. Browse the merchandise while you wait, or do what we do in New Orleans--talk to other people who are waiting. Breathe, man--Central Grocery smells like heaven. And it's smelled exactly that way since I first came in here as a child. The air is worth five stars. Is there a six star rating? They should charge for the air, but they don't. How fast do you think a small place can make perfect sandwiches, each like the last, that everyone seems to want? Don't arrive at 4:59p and expect to be served--Jesus, these people haven't stopped for 8 hours--the line has to end sometime and they need to go home. They need to go home and reflect positively on the day, so they will get the hell out of bed and come back the next day and keeping making sandwiches! God knows they could probably retire, but they don't. And I kiss the ground they walk on that they still open the doors everyday! So skip the Zeno's paradox business and go a healthy spell before 5pm to get your sandwiches. Like 2pm.

text: I've been driving by the makings of this place for almost two years now on my way to and from work. After the first few months, I started looking for the "open" sign to be on. Month after month of no sign, I started to give up hope. Meanwhile, my thoughts were that it was clearly going to be a Qdoba or Chipotle-style place, and the only way they'd get a leg up on those businesses (besides being local, if you're into that) is same quality food with better prices, or better food and similar prices. The place finally opened this past Monday, and a few of us ventured in there today so as to avoid opening-day chaos of 50% off food. What a letdown. I hate giving negative reviews, but I give this place six months. Besides the spotty service, (I'll get to that) the food was VERY mediocre and kinda scary. The chicken was marinated in something that made it orangy-pink, and it was mealy. The guacamole definitely came out of a bag, not from a fresh avocado. The salsas were all from a can or jar. I got the quesadilla, which they steamed (???) rather than grilled, then didn't cut it. It was a gooey mess that was difficult to eat with both fork and hand. Service was odd, not lazy. They have plenty of people on the line, but depending on what people ordered, some people were going around ahead of us if their stuff got ready sooner. Not a biggie, just disorganized. I had to ask for guac and salsa which the menu lists comes with the meal. (upon which she tried to tell me guac was extra--which I know it is on certain items, but not this one!!) Free stale chips & salsa with your order today. Yay. I'm all for supporting local fare--when it's good and prompt. Unfortunately, Spice Fresh is either not yet on their A game, or this is just par for the course. I'd love to let the owner defend himself, because maybe some of these things are kinks yet to be worked out, but it seems like one would open with your best foot forward, so I'm guessing this is what to expect.

Despite arriving on time - and having reservations, nothing was available. We were told by the lovelies at the front desk that four parties were still working on their entre's so we could wait outside and have a drink if we wanted??? That's not what we wanted to hear particularly since it was July's hottest evening on record. We were standing there trying to decide if we should just walk across the street to one of the dozen other restaurants, when the hostess said, "oh, we can seat you now". HUH? Despite their disorganization, we were quite happy. From here on in, everyting was basically fine, that's it, just fine. The waiter brought our appetizers and (less than) one minute later, he was back with our entrees. I remarked that "usually there is a few minute gap between the two - and he did offer to have them "sit" in the kitchen. Nevermind, we'll take them now. The food was fine, nothing special. I can't say that I found the decor to be very mexican - it was certainly comfortable, but the whole evening didn't feel authentic. Although the waitstaff, for the most part, are mexican - and very personable. Will we go back? Nope. There is a lot better within a mile in any direction.

text: I'm torn between wanting everyone to know how awesome I think this place is and wanting to keep it a secret all to myself. A delicious way to get some ruffage in (if you know what I mean). This is what I've had so far: Easy Caprese- a caprese sammie on some delicious bread pressed to perfection. I gobbled up every bit of it. Washington Turkey- apples and cheese with my turkey? yes, please. ON scrumptious bread? yes, please. I've had several sandwiches that try to incorporate cheese and apples. This is by far the best attempt. Again, I gobbled up every last bite. Cuban sandwich- This is my lunch today... like right now... seriously. I don't think that they make it with pulled pork anymore as mine looked sliced, but it was still delicous. With all the rich tasting meats, it tasted kind of like the offspring of the Cuban and Reuban but with the Cuban having the more dominant genes. OK, I guess you just learned I majored in biology. Anyways, very good. I'm fighting to not finish the other half. And the only reason I'm not gobbling it down is because I got a freshly baked slice of their Java banana cake. Sigh- so sinful! This time they topped it with chocolate chips. Yes, their sandwiches aren't the cheapest around but the really are a good price for what you're getting: a made-to-order pressed sammie with quality ingredients and a side included. Besides, they have a loyalty card: every $10 spent you get a punch and after 5 punches you get a $10 gift card. So you get $10 back for every $50 spent! Ladies, beware. Today there was a rather dashing looking fellow with a very nice Irish accent working there. I'm taken, but if you're single I believe his name is Jason and I'm sure you'll know who he is when you walk in :) Finally, try their tropical mango iced tea. So "refreshing" as my friend would say. A perfect treat for any time since we live in Florida.

text: LOVED IT!!! CAPT NOLAN IS THE BEST! Now that I am done shouting, let me begin by saying that as a New Yorker, I was under the impression that the swamps would be stagnant, gross and full of mosquitoes, especially during the time of year that my friends and I went, which was last week, late July. Well, I could not have been more wrong. They were absolutely gorgeous! We opted for the covered boat because the sun was intense the day we went. I probably took no less than 100 photos during the tour, 50 of which were just of the surroundings. Cypress trees, spanish moss, beautiful white spider lillies, the water, etc. Nature rules. As for getting there , we did not take the bus - we rented a car, and for the 5 of us to rent an SUV for the day, it was a total bargain. So we drove to Slidell, made the 5PM tour, and did not have to deal with the bus situation which is apparently shitty according to other Yelpers. As for the tour, we had Capt. Nolan as our guide. He was awesome - we really could not have asked for a better guide. He was funny, knowledgeable, and genuine. A guy you could have a few beers with. It was clear that even though we were his 5th tour of the day, he truly enjoyed giving the tour and educating folks about the area, the whole boat shared a lot of laughs. He even put up with the 50 million questions I asked, all with a genuine smile. I wrote about the flora, but as for fauna, we saw (and fed) a couple of small gators and a rather large one, even some wild boars (or were they pigs? what do I know?), birds, etc. It was odd that you feed them marshmallows and hot dogs, but they seemed to enjoy them, so who am I to judge? Yes, you get to hold a baby alligator. Truly a great experience. Will be back, and will do another tour with Cajun Encounters. It was nice to get out of the craziness of the city and into some serene settings with a great captain to lead the way. I definitely recommend this tour, and I highly recommend going there yourself by renting a car. We did a few of the plantations the same day also, and driving yourself is so much better. Not only is it cheaper, but it is always nice to do things at your own pace.

text: Oooof. My first one-star review. It's painful, but I have to say that Fuku Sushi truly deserves it. It was my first time dining there, and that was because one of my girlfriends was having a birthday dinner. I didn't have high hopes, but I certainly wasn't ready for the utter disappointment either. I walk into the place, and it's full of frat boys and sorority girls. Okay, that's fine. No biggie. It's the weekend before the undergrads start. But then, I realized that this place had a bit of an identity crisis. Are you a restaurant? Or are you a club? The music was blasting, and the lights were dimmed down. The token creepy older men were there to check out girls who were barely of age. I had to scream to talk to people sitting across from me. Okay, fine. Well maybe the food is half-decent. So, my fiance and I ordered six pieces of nigiri: salmon, yellowtail, and red snapper. We also ordered a yellowtail scallion roll. Not a big order. I know they were busy. I saw that they were pretty much packed. But at the same time, it's a tiny place, and I expected them to be fully staffed for a Friday night before the undergrad school year starts. Anyway, we waited about an hour for our sushi. Plus, our yellowtail scallion roll was plated on someone else's plate. Luckily that person was our friend and just sitting across from us, but still! I took one look at that roll, and it literally was just yellowtail and green onions, with rice, wrapped in seaweed. No pizzazz. The roll was poorly made, with some pieces having little to no fish, just green onion. To add insult to injury, the nigiri was bad. The fish wasn't fresh. My fiance LOVES salmon, and he said that it was the worst he's ever had. He said that this place is 3x worse than Ra, and that is saying a lot. We quickly learned that this place was NOT a place for sushi. Well, the drink situation wasn't much better. We ordered sake bombs for almost all 15 of us because it was my girlfriend's birthday, and we were in a drinking mood. The Asahi beer came in large bottles, and the warm sake was on the side. The beer wasn't cold. It was only chilled. We dealt with it. Then, when a couple of boys started to just sip the sake, they said that it tasted watered down. I took a sip myself, and I had to agree. Either it was watered down or they just buy the cheapest sake they could find. I was saddened that they couldn't even get that part right. Lastly, they didn't keep the women's restroom fully stocked with disposable sanitary seat covers or toilet paper. So I had to wait a few minutes for the employee to put in more toilet paper, and the sanitary seat cover holder remained empty. Also, the men's restroom lock doesn't work. In conclusion, I will not be returning. I'm also not sure what kind of demographic this restaurant-club is trying to appeal to...undergrads that don't know what sushi is? Or undergrads who just don't care? Either way, for a business to be successful, they need to uphold good quality product no matter who they are planning to serve, and if they don't, more people are going to take their money elsewhere.

text: I have been to Village Pizza at least 3-4 times over the last 2-3 months, and maybe a total of 8-10 times since I first entered Philadelphia, back in 2009. But it is more out of necessity (aka, late at night and just needing nourishment before getting back to studying for that exam the next morning). To be honest, this is an average pizza shop, with okay food and ample seating. The one thing that tends to plague the pizza shops in this area is that they are right next to Drexel University's residential community. Which essentially means that they can put slop on a platter and serve it as food, with minimal repercussions or complaints. Village Pizza is no exception to this rule. The cheese pizza is too oily/greasy for my taste, and the jalapeño poppers are clearly the ones that were bought at Costco, removed from the freezer, and fried. Not that that's the end of the world - I mean, I wasn't expecting freshly made poppers for a mere 4.80, but still, they managed to mess up the simple act of frying. Somehow, the same batch managed to have two poppers that were still cold in the center, and 3 others that were charred. Personally, I'm really unsure as to how you can deep fry stuff unevenly, but I guess they know the trick! The vegetable pizza was definitely better than the cheese one, but just marginally. The spinach ricotta was extremely unappealing visually, but tasted good (and didn't give you the impression that it would cause you to have a heart attack). If anything, some of the non-pizza items on the menu look a tad bit more palatable, but I've stayed cautious and never tried them before. They seem to be using the same grill for everything, and given the fact that I am (mostly) a vegetarian, I figured that this would be more prudent.

text: Corner pub feel in an area of the city that is lacking in corner pubs. It's small, narrow, and built for having a few beers and eating pub grub while sitting at the bar. The interior of the place feels like an english pub and when you walk out of the place onto the cobblestone 2nd street you may think you have actually gone back in time...but don't worry, there is a wawa just down the street to bring you back to reality and provide you with some snacks to stumble home with. The draft list is limited but respectable, the bottle list makes up for the limited draft selection. The benefit of the draft list is that beers are poured in imperial pints in traditional English style, so you get to enjoy an extra 4oz compared to most bars in the city. The downside is that a Troegs Sunshine Pils cost $6...not bad, but not a great deal either. They do have the MLB package and you can claim a TV to watch out of town games...and I think you can actually call ahead to reserve a TV to watch a game. Overall, it's a cool spot. I'll put it on my list of regular haunts.

text: For what it is, T-Bowl hits the spot. I came in on opening day to long lines and disoriented folks. Despite the clear disorganized nature that typically accompanies first days, T-Bowl appears to be something that will actually be here for the long run in Penn's famed "cursed" business location. You chose between white rice or organic brown and then throw in a variety of add-ins for $1. I skipped on the meat option and stuck with edamame, red peppers, and snow peas. The sauce is where T-Bowl has to make a serious decision: are we makin' salads here, people, or are we doing stir fry? The sheer number of sauces/dressings/etc. is a little confounding considering stir fry is normally cooked with a very limited number of sauce-like options. I foolishly selected a lemon flavored sauce and ended up with something I would have enjoyed more on a salad. I'm sure if I stuck with something traditional like a teriyaki or a sweet and sour sauce, the food would have been better. Yet, the food was still very good. Fresh ingredients and organic rice in a bowl they bring out to you sounds excellent to me. The portions are perfect for lunch, and although there is some chatter about it's high prices, I think since us students spend around $5 at a food truck, $8 for something fresher is warranted. Oh-and get the fried egg! PS. They only had one bubble tea flavor at the time, which was coffee-ish. I would have preferred green tea, but the drink is refreshing and fun, if a drink can be fun.

text: I have to admit I'm a sushi addict so I can't stand mediocre sushi, no matter the price. I make an almost yearly pilgrimage to Japan just to eat sushi. The miso itself tasted ok, but the sea weed was still semi dehydrated. Almost like they threw in dried seawood 10 seconds before serving me the soup. Completely unacceptable for such an easy dish to make. The sushi was ok. Not bad, but definitely not memorable. Any place that has a million rolls and not much nigiri means usually means their fish isn't the freshest. Rolls are an easy way to cover up the fish, unlike nigiri which you can't cover up the lack of quality and freshness. The rice could have used a little more vinegar. Kinda bland. The maguro was stringy. You have to eat it while since you couldn't bite it in half. The scallop didn't taste the freshest. Had a slight fishy flavor which is never good. Raw shellfish is really critical that it's fresh. The rolls were alright. But you couldn't really taste the fish with all the sauce or Panko crumbs they throw in there. In all fairness, what should I have expected eating sushi in the French quarter. Would I eat here again? Maybe. Only since there is no other sushi restaurant in the area.

text: Busch gardens!! Personally, I love animals and natural-looking/natural surroundings over fake man-made colorful buildings. This place is so beautiful! The rides here are far better than the rides at Disney. Disney is AWESOME of course. Each park is great in its own way. This park is more geared towards wildlife, animals, and ROLLER COASTERS. There are different themes in this park such as Morocco, Egypt/desert, jungle, African, etc. Now, ROLLER COASTERS!! If you are a thrill-seeker like me, here is a list of rides you need to go on: Sheikra (must go at least twice lol), Kumba, Gwazi (awesome wooden coaster), and Montu. Those are my faves in that order. Yes there are more rides to choose from, but those were my faves. Scorpian was alright...I went on that last and after the rides prior, it was nothing. Another ride I would recommend is more laid back compared to those coasters...Congo River Rapids. Expect to get a little wet or maybe a lot..depends on where you sit and how lucky you are haha. There was an area in the "Edge of Africa" section of the park where you could go to the large glass window, and tigers would come right up to you as if they wanted to take a picture with you lol. There are several areas in the park where there are animals around you as if you were at a zoo. You can go on safari rides (one for an additional cost). There was a show we watched --I think it was at the Marrakesh Theater--not sure...but it was spectacular! So many different costumes and settings, colors were amazing, music was great, dancing and singing performances were beautiful. I think they change their shows every so often, but the show we watched was about old folk tales. We also watched a 4D movie at the Timbuktu Theater. It was cute. 4D=3D movie with glasses and getting lightly sprayed/misted with water. We ate at the Desert Grill. There were live singing and dancing performances here. It's basically a huge place with a stage for shows and picnic tables for the audience to eat and watch. There is a section for choosing/ordering/buying your food...kind of like a cafeteria. If you are sick of Disney and want to shake things up a bit, this is a great place to go to! I really enjoyed this place and I've been to all the Disney parks..this place is refreshing! =) Oh and here's a tip...this place has sister parks: SeaWorld, Aquatica, Discovery Cove, and Adventure Island. Go find discounts if you plan on going to more than one of these parks!! =)

text: Best park in the world! Hands down. Central Park in NYC, Boston Common, Garden of Heavenly Gardens in Suzhou, China, wherever else there's a park in the world- it doesn't matter. Nowhere else do u see these GORGEOUS centuries old oak trees. And the fact that City Park's so huge! 5th largest urban park in the nation! I love exploring Couterie Forest and pretending I'm miles away instead of being in the heart of the city. Yet somehow, you no longer hear the sounds of city life and instead focus on the chirping birds, buzzing insects and gurgling from the bayou. You can even climb the highest hill in the city! (Stole that title from Monkey Hill after Katrina.) There are stairs to reach the top or a pretty steep incline to go up. Either way, the Park will supply the oxygen tanks to assist you in reaching the top. Or you can play it safe and stay on the ground. Walk along the many bayou paths or fishing piers. Then you round a bend and find the perfect spot to write your next New York Times bestseller. Or read one of them. Or paint. As always, Nature is the perfect inspiration for everything. And City Park delivers that and more! Love all the strategically placed benches and big tree branches all throughout those deserted paths. My dogs and I love spending our weekends exploring those hidden thoroughfares. We also love City Bark. Best dog park in the city. Love the swimming pools and big drinking area with lots of different sized bowls. My two pups are quite small so they are intimidated by the bigger bowls. But City Bark always accommodates. Love all the sitting areas, under shade, and scattered throughout the large area. Definitely worth price of admission! The the first time I saw it, I knew the Peristyle would be where I have my wedding. It's truly a magical place that always take my breath away. With the last portion of Bayou Metairie remaining in the city, the Peristyle is unique in so many ways. It's a big neo-classical open-air pavilion that has the best acoustics of any outdoor place I know. Toward its back, there are these two huge white lion statues that overlook the bayou. Every kid that visits must climb on it to take pictures. Or they'll clamor down to feed the ducks or swans that flock around steps leading to the bayou. There's always something to see or do right by the Peristyle. And it's just a small portion of City Park! I even loved working here one winter 8 years ago. I helped out with Celebration in the Oaks, their annual fundraiser that's the Christmas lights display throughout the park. (It helps raise 20% of their annual money. They get nothing from the city and very little from the state. The rest they have to fundraise. For one of America's oldest urban parks.) It was a great winter and job. I still dream about working for City Park. Great staff and volunteers who really care about the park and its future. They all have their heart in the right place. Prior to Katrina, Celebration in the Oaks was a driving tour in addition to the walking tour. Now, it's only the walking tour of all the holidays lights. However, it's still a sight to behold and lots of funs to walk through for everyone. Lots for children and adults so families can enjoy it; there's a romantic moonlight strolls for couples; lots of fun activities for groups and individuals. If you've got little kids, you need to check out the life-sized models of nursery tale characters in Storyland. They're great to climb on or into! Kids and adults will also enjoy all the rides- bumper cars are still my favorite. But I love seeing the carousel and riding a flying horse. This place definitely brings out my inner child And I try to take a train ride as much as I can. Riding underneath all those beautiful oaks is one of my favorite activities to do in the city. Next to the gondola rides. If only Venice will be this romantic. Guess I'll have to find out! The Botanical Gardens are the perfect place to eat my lunches. I loved sitting by the modern statues and Roman fountains smelling the sweet honeysuckle. It was always my favorite part of the day. City Park, you are THE reason New Orleans is my home. What an understated gem!

text: I like to eat sushi. And I hang out with a lot of men who like to eat sushi. These men like to consume food in monsterous amounts. Which is why I practically live at Sapporo. The fish is fresh and always prepared and presented nicely. I adore the staff and they are excellent and attentive. They have a large menu capable of pleasing even my seafood-hating friends. And the price ain't bad either. They also offer a menu (which I have to admit, I have never tried) but I know the menu has an even wider assortment of foods beyond what is offered on the buffet. Sapporo doesn't offer a separate all-you-can-eat pricing for lunch and dinner - so no matter when you go, the price is the same - $23 per person. However the menu is always the same too. The only limits they place on their order are the sashimi, the baked oyster, and the baked seafood, which is understandable in my eyes. There is a limit of 20 pieces of sashimi per person. Plus I've eaten here a few times a month for the past couple of years, and I have never once gotten sick. Highfive! They offer a wide assortment of maki and cones, as well as hot food such as tempura (veg and shrimp), spring rolls, chicken and beef teriyaki soups and much more. They are an all you can eat place, but they do expect you to eat what you order and will charge you a few bucks if you don't (they just wrap it up and you take it home). They do this for obvious reasons and I can't say I have any quams with it. The restaurant is located in a shifty area of town, just east of the hospital and kind of in an alley off of 101st. I have never had any problems before (and I've been coming here since this location opened) but I have SEEN homeless people in the area. The inside of the restaurant is simple but quite nice - lots of seating and they are good with groups (however each person at the table must be having all-you-can-eat - I don't see how this is a problem as I can imagine people ripping them off if they didn't stick to this rule). Reservations are very helpful, especially for weekend nights, but I have walked in with a large group of 8 with no notice (it was an accident! I swear!) and they were super accomodating and very friendly. Let's be realistic here. We live in Edmonton, not Vancouver (or a city with an ocean). This sushi is not five star unbelievable. text: As a deeply committed omnivore with a disproportionate number of vegetarian and vegan friends, I often find myself in a culinary quandary - where to go? What to order? Given the current restaurant scene's emphasis on small plates and sharing with friends, I often have to choose between attempting to eat through non-vegetarian options on my lonesome - or get stuck choosing from the limited vegetarian/vegan options available on standard menus. When a vegetarian friend told me she was headed to Philly for a visit, I snagged a reservation at Vedge knowing that this was somewhere we'd both be happy with our meal. The ambiance is lovely - it feels like a special-occasion restaurant without being overly stuffy. Service was stellar - our waiter was very attentive and gave great suggestions, water glasses were never empty, and the bartender even tweaked our cocktails to our specifications (and by "specifications" I mean my vague comment that I don't care for bitters but thought one of the cocktails sounded good, could something be made that was similar but without the bitters? The answer is that bartenders know cocktails way better than you do so just let them do their thing and drink what they give you). Our meal started with two small plates - I had the sweet potato pate and my friend had the salt roasted gold beets. Both of us ordered these with some trepidation and were pleasantly surprised - they were delicious! The sweet potato had a great depth of flavor. My only complaint is that it was served with two small slices of bread, when the portion of the pate was fairly large. I am certain I could have received more bread if I had asked, but I took it as a sign that I should save room for further courses. The golden beets were very light and delicious - especially the creamy cucumber sauce. We also each ordered a larger plate - I had a crepe with hearts of palm, garbanzo beans, and lentils. I challenge any carnivore to eat this and tell me that a dish needs meat to be satisfying. It was delicious and filling and the crepe had a great texture. My friend chose a dish of radishes served several ways - it was very interesting to taste all of the different flavors. It was a much lighter plate, but given the amount of food we had consumed at this point we were happy to have an easy dish! We also ordered 3 plates from the daily "dirt list" - I'd be happy to make a meal of all of the selections from this menu of seasonal veggies! We tried not to go crazy, so we stuck with the crispy cauliflower, brussels sprouts, and fingerling fries with worcestershire sauce. The cauliflower was very good - anywhere else it would have been a favorite, but here it just had too much competition. Same for the fingerling "fries." The hands-down favorite, though, were the brussels sprouts - we could not believe that the delicious creamy sauce was vegan. Vedge has redeemed the existance of veganaise for me: if it can be made into something this delicious, it can be allowed to continue to exist. Vedge really is a spot where everyone will end up happy. It's great to be able to choose a dinner spot without having to run the menu by everyone to make sure they'll have sufficient choices - vegan, vegetarians, pescetarians, omnivores, and carnivores alike will all be blown away by Vedge's animal-product-free offerings.

text: I've come to my own conclusion that Ann Dancing as an attempt at art is a fail. I know art. I've regularly visited the IMA, been to public releases, heard artists speak about their work, and how excited they are when their attempt at a message is conveyed. I also am able to tie pieces to points, in time, important events, emotions, or messages. However, Ann's display is merely that, a display. Lack of color, (and actually bad animation) make this seem more of an attempt at a shock value piece, and even then does not display a message that is shocking, new or unattempted. This could have been done by a fourth grader with an Etch-A-Sketch Animate. It does not push the limits of art, but rather uses dated technology and a very boring subject. I see enough "Ann's" dancing on Mass Ave anyway. Furthermore, this is a waste of resources. The electricity used to power this piece is wasted just on the display of the piece. There is no other thing this piece is powering or illuminating. The other resources are the LED display itself. It requires precious rare earths to make these flat panel displays we love. And at the rate we are pouring through them, we will run out before we can recycle them into new displays. So as a city landmark resource, it is a waste.

text: I've eaten here three times: twice for dinner and once for the buffet. I totally don't agree that this is the "best in Indy." I think it's fairly similar to other Northern Indian restaurants like Shalimar or India Garden--but with a fatal flaw. Read on. THE GOOD For dinner, they bring out tasty papad and chutney. For dinner and lunch, they bring out a generous basket of piping hot nan. It's A- nan in my book, but it's fresh (unlike the nan of many other establishments who leave the bread to languish on the buffet). The food is of pretty good quality. The staff is cheery and attentive. So what's not to dig? THE BAD The food is SALTY, man! It just destroys me. My girlfriend and I split a fish pakora and a goat curry for dinner recently, and I think we lowered the water table because we were drinking so much. Crying out for ¡EL AGUA! Yes, Indian food is not usually your first choice for low-sodium fare. But having half an appetizer and entree and feeling that bad is unacceptable. It's a shame, as their food is pretty well-prepared, otherwise. For example, the ajwain seeds in the fish pakora were a nice touch (by the way, I think the majority of the saltitude was in the curry, not the pakora). THE BUFFET People have given the lunch buffet high marks. I had it today and was unimpressed. There was no more variety than at your typical Indian joint in town. There were no dishes that really blew me away. It was just average--except SALTIER than average. (In fact, I tested out the buffet today even after my previous, salty experiences precisely because so many people were lauding it.) For Indian food in Indy, I recommend Passage to India (my favorite--vegetarian with lots of Southern food, great soups), India Palace (huge lunch buffet with substantial meat dishes), Taj of India (simple but good quality for lunch or dinner), and Shalimar (decent lunch buffet, nice dinner service with good thali).

text: I didn't expect to review a Red Wing shoe store. I frankly didn't expect to have a bad experience, I knew what size I was, what I wanted and basically wanted to be in an out without too much fuss. I realize the store operates 98% of it's time providing shoes for people who need specialty heavy-duty boots. I was in the 2% of people who go in there for a pair of good boots that will last me a long time - but don't necessarily "need" them. I am still of the opinion that Red Wing makes a quality product, but unfortunately I don't foresee me setting foot in one of their stores ever again. I'll stick to the basics and if for some odd reason the gentleman working in the store reads this - to help him clarify what happened that night. I walk in at about 7PM on October 23rd, 2012 - I don't know the name of the person working there - since I was never greeted, but it's not the end of the world. He's with two other clients and I can tell the guy is busy. I walk around trying to kill time and to give him time to get wrapped up - I'm in no hurry. I understand it's not the most ideal scenario and I don't expect them to drop everything they're doing - although, I can't think how "Hi, I'll be with you in a minute." would have cost him any time, but that's besides the point. A bunch of unacknowledged nothing happens after that I could be going around the store setting small fires and I doubt anything would be said to me. He completes the transaction with the first client, and I can tell he now needs to help client number two. I say nothing, I just happen to be near him towards the back of the store by the sizing machine. Suddenly, he snaps at me and says "You're GOING TO have to give me a minute DUDE - I'm the only one here." Keep in mind, I said nothing at this point. I am giving him a minute, in fact - I gave him twenty. Great first acknowledgement. I'm not the big traditionalist when it comes to customer service, and I'm not blind - I know you're busy. But if your first words to me are in that tone, then you lost a sale. It really isn't a problem you see - you don't want my business, and I don't want to give it to you. It actually works out perfectly for the both of us. This isn't the only source of Red Wing boots, and although I was set on the brand. Now I think I'm willing to give my other options a shot - and I mean that, I know it doesn't matter to this particular dealer, and I'm fine with that. . Of course, the boots I was looking for - Model 8146, are available at Brooks Brothers and I can tell you, the service there would be eons apart from this store. If so inclined, I may just drop by - but I really think there are too many options now that this sent me right back to the internet to look at what other alternatives there are out there. I appreciate someone is out there making an American made product, in American small business like these franchised Red Wing stores (dealerships) - I want to support that. But unfortunately, it's not worth the hassle of being treated like a nuisance.

text: A great value for the money. The unit I have is spacious and well layed out for a one bedroom (720 sq ft). There is a small storage unit on the nice sized balcony, double closet in hall, counter space and cabs in bathroom, and a walk in closet. There is more storage than many 1 bd I looked at. Wooden shutters are a nice touch. The staff are friendly, helpful, and prompt. Maintenance staff are prompt, do a good job, and leave the place clean after they are done. I love that I can do requests online and pay rent/water online. Has a good mix of residents - families, college students, retirees, etc., and is quiet. I actually have a great view from my unit as well. Complex is definitely older, but well maintained. Parking is adequate, though not assigned, but spaces are large - no door dings. Office is open daily (Sundays till 3 p.m.) so it's convenient. The Pool/Hot Tub has never not worked since I've been here. They offer a smallish gym, and a decent laundry room which are keyed, as is the pool area. Laundry does not take coins, but a refillable "debit" card, so office hours are convenient for this. Old tennis courts are being taken out and replaced with a fenced pet park. If there are any cons: kitchens are quite small, not a lot of counter space; no microwave provided; no assigned parking/covered parking; no laundry inside units; grills are not gas. There are great views of the Catalinas, and a wash right behind the property you can "hike" in; and the buildings are up/down hills, so good for walking to/from laundry, mail boxes, office, etc. The complex is situated on good routes to all areas of town and is near to shopping, restaurants, malls, and hospitals. Very convenient to most everything/easy to get from here to there. This is not "luxury" but it's very livable and they keep it well maintained. For the price, you likely won't find better, especially to mention the attentive staff. I didn't give it 4 stars for being modern, flashy, or like a resort ... but for price, affordability, everything being in working order, prompt, reliable staff, well maintained, quiet community, privacy respected, and no negative issues with my unit or enjoyment of it. If you have a child going to college, you could feel good about them being here.

text: I was booked here for a writer's night over 3 months ago, and when I arrived, I was told I was not on the list. Not only that, but my violinist had already made the trip from Memphis. Great. The Bluebird may be historical, but that gives the staff no right to be snotty, pretentious, and BEYOND rude. I have played at many "historical" venues, including where Elvis played his first show & where Johnny Cash played his first show and have never dealt with people that were THIS full of themselves. When my family came to see me play last time, my dad had the privilege of nursing one of their lukewarm beers for over 3 hours. Super. The sound is mediocre, to say the best, and is certainly not the best live sound in Nashville. However, the sound engineer and bartender were the only hospitable people that entire night. I was pleasantly surprised when I walked in the door and the girl in charge of seating people greeted me with a smile. I asked her where there was a free table and she told me that she didn't work there. Figures. The actual host came and was promptly as rude as I remember always being treated at The Bluebird. Since this was the FOURTH time my entire party of folks and I have been treated badly by the Bluebird, we left. I called the manager at Taps and Tapas, and he fit us in for a last minute show that night. I will never be playing the Bluebird again. Go to Belcourt Taps and Tapas if you wanted to be treated like a human being. If you'd rather be treated like an unworthy imbecile, go to The Bluebird.

The calamari was more rubbery than usual. Everything was off. It was a real let down. 4. Location is ok but if I were so close to the beach, I would have tried a location down that way. For someone who works up the street from this place, my boyfriend didn't even know where it was. Doesn't have a real presence yet. 5. The service was medicore. I know Ceviche isn't known for a southern hospitality style service but I've seen better service from other locations especially from the wait staff. I think I'm out of reasons. My boyfriend's mom really wants to try Ceviche the next time she's in town. After visiting this location, he knows to take her to the S. Tampa location instead.
